As we wrap up our time with *Consider the Lobster and Other Essays*, let’s take a moment to appreciate what you’ve just done. You’ve looked beyond the obvious, been willing to sit with uncertainty, and explored ideas most people never even notice. These essays aren’t just witty observations—they’re invitations. Invitations to live a little more thoughtfully, to pay attention to what’s hidden, and to care about the things that truly matter.
So, what can you carry with you from here? Remember to notice those small details. Sometimes, they’ll reveal the biggest truths. Don’t just accept the stories you’re told—especially the comfortable ones. Practice empathy, even when it feels hard or inconvenient. Notice how language shapes your world, and choose your words with care and curiosity. Be willing to challenge what’s expected—even if you’re the only one standing. And it’s okay if some questions don’t have easy answers.
Seek meaning in your everyday moments, not just in big achievements. Let yourself be vulnerable—because authenticity is always worth it. Stay awake to the way media and culture shape how you see things. And above all, keep asking questions, even when the world says you shouldn’t.
Life is layered, strange, and sometimes full of contradictions. It’s tempting to get lost in all the noise or settle for easy answers. But you don’t have to. You can choose to look closer, to listen deeper, and to live with more awareness.
This isn’t about being perfect. It’s about being present, curious, and kind—with yourself, and with others.
The work of understanding and empathy is never really finished. But every small effort matters. So, head out into the world with open eyes and an open heart. The details—they’re waiting for you.
